subject: Culture
title: Food Offerings to Gods
description: A micro-lesson that makes Food Offerings to Gods usable.

hook.text: In Bali, Hindu families place tiny offerings of rice and flowers on the ground three times daily.

buildup.text: Food offerings appear in ancient Greece, China, Egypt, and Mesoamerica. Gods always eat first.

discovery.text: In Japanese Shinto, food placed at shrines is later eaten by the family. The gods take the essence.

twist.text: Day of the Dead altars feature the deceased's favorite foods. The dead still have taste preferences.

climax.text: Offering food to the invisible world is humanity's oldest shared ritual. It predates every religion.

punchline.text: We fed the gods before we named them.

quiz.question: In Japanese Shinto tradition, what happens to food placed at shrines?
